cantonalMultiplier.note: This is the INCOME tax coefficient annuel for 2026 (96% of Art. 37 al. 1 LICD table rates, per Art. 1 al. 1 LCA2026). The WEALTH tax coefficient annuel for 2026 is SEPARATELY set at 100% (Art. 1 al. 2 LCA2026) -- i.e. no scaling needed this year, the wealthTaxBrackets above already ARE the final effective cantonal rates. Both coefficients are re-set annually by the Grand Conseil and are NOT guaranteed to stay at these values in future years; a developer must keep them as two independent parameters, not a single canton-wide multiplier.

notes:
MECHANISM -- THREE INDEPENDENT LAYERS ON ONE SHARED BASE: FR computes a single reference amount, the 'impot cantonal de base' (base/simple tax), from the Art. 37 LICD income barème or Art. 62 LICD wealth barème. THREE separate percentage multipliers are then each applied directly to that SAME base amount (not chained/compounded on each other): (1) the CANTONAL 'coefficient annuel' -- 96% for income, 100% for wealth, for fiscal year 2026 (Art. 1 LCA2026, RSF 631.12) -- this is cantonalMultiplier above; (2) the COMMUNAL coefficient, set annually by each municipality, capped by law (Art. 4 LICo) at 100% of the base (up to 125% exceptionally with Conseil d'Etat approval), and by law MUST be IDENTICAL for income and wealth tax (Art. 4 al. 3 LICo) -- see municipalMultiplier in FR_municipalities.json; (3) the ECCLESIASTICAL/PARISH coefficient, set annually by each parish, capped at 20% of the base for natural persons (Art. 16 LEE), and UNLIKE the communal layer is legally free to differ between income and wealth (confirmed empirically, e.g. commune Avry: catholic parish charges 4.5% on income but 15.0% on wealth -- see churchMultiplierCatholic vs churchMultiplierCatholicWealth in FR_municipalities.json). A taxpayer's total bill = base*(cantonal% + communal% + church%) computed independently per tax type (income vs wealth), NOT base*cantonal% then +communal%-of-that-scaled-result.

INCOME TAX IS A FORMULA/AVERAGE-RATE SCHEDULE, NOT A DISCRETE MARGINAL TABLE (same family of mechanism as Valais/Neuchatel elsewhere in this project): Art. 37 al. 1 LICD legally defines income tax via 10 income classes plus a flat top rate, where the AVERAGE tax rate increases LINEARLY with income WITHIN each class (from a stated start-% to a stated end-%), then jumps slightly to the next class's start-%, and above CHF 207'100 (single) the average rate is flat at 13.5%. The 10 official class boundaries and average-rate endpoints (singles) are: [5'200-17'499]: 1.0000%->4.1598%; [17'500-31'399]: 4.1745%->6.2031%; [31'400-48'299]: 6.2139%->8.0283%; [48'300-63'799]: 8.0352%->9.0978%; [63'800-77'599]: 9.1042%->9.9810%; [77'600-102'099]: 9.9846%->10.8630%; [102'100-128'699]: 10.8662%->11.7142%; [128'700-155'999]: 11.7172%->12.5332%; [156'000-180'999]: 12.5355%->13.1082%; [181'000-207'099]: 13.1097%->13.4997%; [207'100+]: flat 13.5000%. Because average rate rises within each class, the TRUE MARGINAL rate is continuously increasing within each class (always higher than the average rate shown) and then DROPS abruptly at 207'100 when the schedule goes flat -- a genuine 'bracket-creep cliff' in the marginal rate, not a data artifact (confirmed: derived marginal rate peaks around ~17% just below CHF 207'100 then drops to the flat 13.5%). DERIVATION METHOD for the {from,rate} breakpoint tables above: the canton publishes its own official pre-computed lookup table giving the exact CHF tax amount at EVERY CHF 100 of income from 5'200 to 414'200 (../sources/FR_bareme_revenu_2023plus.pdf / .txt, 4091 rows, parsed programmatically), for both the single and married columns. We split each of the 10 legal classes (doubled for married, see below) into 3 equal sub-intervals and computed the exact average marginal rate within each sub-interval as (tax_hi - tax_lo)/(income_hi - income_lo) using the government's own published amounts -- i.e. a piecewise-CONSTANT approximation of a truly piecewise-LINEAR marginal-rate curve. Validated by re-summing across all 4091 grid points: max absolute error is CHF 10.91 (single, worst case at CHF 11'400 income) and CHF 24.74 (married, worst case at CHF 22'700 income) -- well under 0.1% of the tax owed at those incomes, and errors shrink further at higher incomes. A developer needing exact-to-the-rappen results should instead implement the official piecewise-linear AVERAGE-rate formula directly using the class endpoints quoted above (tax(x) = x * avgRate(x)/100, with avgRate linear-interpolated within each class) rather than relying solely on these breakpoints. Income below CHF 5'200 has no published table row; we assumed the canton's own stated 'taux minimal'/'taux minimum' of 1.0000% applies flat down to CHF 0 (bracket {from:0,rate:0.01}) -- this is an assumption, not directly confirmed for the 0-5'200 range specifically (the 'taux minimal' language in Art. 37 al. 3 LICD is stated in the context of the splitting floor, see below), so a developer should double check whether truly zero income is taxed at all once social deductions are applied (which happens upstream of this bracket table and is not part of this dataset).

MARRIED/SPLITTING QUIRK (Art. 37 al. 3 LICD): couples taxed jointly (and single-parent/support households) are NOT taxed on a separately-legislated married schedule -- instead, the applicable AVERAGE RATE is the rate that the SINGLE schedule would produce for HALF the couple's combined taxable income, and that rate is then applied to the FULL income: rate_married(x) = rate_single(x/2), tax_married(x) = x * rate_single(x/2). This was verified exactly against the government's own published married-column table: e.g. rate_married(414'200) = 13.5000% = rate_single(207'100) to 4 decimal places, confirming the doubled class boundaries used above (2x each single-schedule threshold) are correct. 'Le taux minimal de l'impot reste applicable' (the minimum 1.0% rate stays the floor) even under this halving. The incomeTaxBrackets.married array here was derived independently via the identical class-subdivision/numerical-differentiation method applied directly to the government's own published married-column tax amounts (not by re-deriving from the single column), so it should match the official married tax amounts to the same accuracy as the single table.

WEALTH TAX -- genuine discrete marginal bracket table (Art. 62 LICD, no formula involved, current cantonal coefficient annuel = 100% so no scaling needed for 2026): 0-50'000: 0.50 permille; 50'001-100'000: 1.10; 100'001-200'000: 1.80; 200'001-400'000: 2.50; 400'001-700'000: 3.10; 700'001-1'000'000: 3.50; 1'000'001-1'200'000: 3.70; above 1'200'000: 2.90 permille. NOTABLE QUIRK: the TOP bracket's marginal rate (2.90 permille) is LOWER than the previous bracket's (3.70 permille) -- a genuine regressive/degressive top bracket confirmed directly from the canton's own official PDF (not a transcription error), evidently a deliberate cap to limit the wealth-tax burden on very large fortunes. Total wealth tax owed still strictly increases with wealth (all rates are positive), it is only the MARGINAL rate that dips at the top.

MUNICIPAL LAYER AND 2025 MERGER WAVE: FR went through a wave of municipal mergers effective largely 1 January 2025 (approved by cantonal parliament / popular vote), reducing the commune count. The canton's own open-data commune-coefficient dataset (opendata.fr.ch '18_03_coefficients', last confirmed update = 2025, no 2026 rows published as of Sept 2026) shows: 2023 = 126 communes, 2024 = 126, 2025 = 121 (after Auboranges+Chapelle(Glane)+Ecublens(FR)+Rue merged into 'Rue', Montet(Glane) absorbed into 'Ursy', and Grolley+Ponthaux merged into 'Grolley-Ponthaux'). A SEVENTH merger (Fetigny + Menieres -> 'Fetigny-Menieres', BFS 2056) is already reflected in the CURRENT official BFS municipality register AND in the 2026 parish/church datasets (which explicitly list 'Fetigny-Menieres' as of 1 Aug 2026) but is NOT yet reflected in the commune-coefficient dataset (which still shows the old separate Fetigny/Menieres 2025 rates, 86.0% and 88.1% respectively) -- so FR_municipalities.json includes 'Fetigny-Menieres' (BFS 2056) with municipalMultiplier=null rather than guessing/averaging the two predecessor rates.

ERRATA (added 2026-09-11): per user request, the null was replaced with municipalMultiplier=87.1 (the average of the two predecessor communes' last known 2025 rates, 86.0% and 88.1%), municipalMultiplierEstimated=true, with the app UI flagging this as an estimate rather than presenting it as a confirmed rate. Must be replaced once the canton's 2026 commune-coefficient dataset actually includes Fetigny-Menieres. Net result: 120 municipalities in FR_municipalities.json for 2026 (121 CSV rows - Fetigny - Menieres + Fetigny-Menieres). Municipal multiplier figures for all other municipalities are 2025 values (the latest published; fr.ch's own coefficients page also had no 2026 dataset available as of this research). SEPARATE QUIRK -- 'ULMIZ': the canton's commune-coefficient dataset still carries an entry for 'Ulmiz' (its own multiplier 85.0% for 2025, materially different from neighbouring Murten's 62.0%) even though the CURRENT official BFS municipality register (bfs_municipalities_register.csv used elsewhere in this project) no longer lists Ulmiz as an independent commune at all (it appears to have been administratively absorbed by Murten around 2016) and NEITHER the reformed NOR catholic parish datasets have any Ulmiz entry. We kept Ulmiz in FR_municipalities.json (using its historical BFS number 2278) with its own municipalMultiplier and church fields left null, but flag this as UNRESOLVED: it may be a legacy 'ancienne commune'/village-fraction sub-rate still levied within Murten's boundary, or a stale row in the canton's own dataset -- a developer should verify directly with the SCC before using it.

CHURCH TAX / PARISH STRUCTURE -- THE HEADLINE QUIRK: FR church tax is levied by INDIVIDUAL PARISHES (Catholic and Reformed separately), and parish boundaries frequently do NOT coincide with political-municipality boundaries -- this is the core reason a flat canton-wide or even a single per-municipality church rate is insufficient. The canton itself publishes two authoritative datasets that pre-resolve parish membership to municipality (opendata.fr.ch '18_03_coefficients_impots_catholiques': 156 rows covering 119 communes; '..._reformes': 124 rows covering 119 communes; both dated 'etat au 1er aout 2026' i.e. already CURRENT for tax year 2026, cross-validated identical against the pre-downloaded FR_coef_paroisses_*_2026.pdf files). For MOST communes exactly one parish (of each confession) covers the whole commune. But for 12 communes (catholic) and 3 communes (reformed) in this dataset, MULTIPLE overlapping parishes cover the SAME commune with GENUINELY DIFFERENT rates -- e.g. commune 'Gibloux' spans FIVE different catholic parishes ranging from 8%/8% to 10%/15% (income/wealth); commune 'Torny' spans 2 catholic parishes (both at an identical 10%/10%, so not actually ambiguous in practice); commune 'Fribourg' (the capital) spans SIX different catholic parishes but by coincidence all six charge the identical 6.0% income / 18.0% wealth rate, so it is NOT ambiguous in practice either. For the communes where the overlapping parishes truly disagree, FR_municipalities.json sets churchMultiplierCatholic/Reformed (and their Wealth counterparts) to null and instead adds a churchNoteCatholic/churchNoteReformed string field listing every overlapping parish name and its exact income/wealth rates -- resolving to a single number would require sub-municipality (street/address-level parish-membership) data that is not available at this granularity; a production calculator needs to ask the user which parish they belong to, or default conservatively. ADDITIONAL QUIRK: unlike the communal coefficient (legally required to be IDENTICAL for income and wealth, Art. 4 al. 3 LICo), the ecclesiastical coefficient has NO such equality requirement (Art. 16 LEE) and empirically often does differ substantially between income and wealth for the SAME parish (e.g. commune Avry catholic parish: 4.5% income vs 15.0% wealth -- over 3x). Because the requested schema field is a single number, FR_municipalities.json stores the INCOME church coefficient in churchMultiplierReformed/Catholic and ADDS two extra non-schema fields, churchMultiplierReformedWealth and churchMultiplierCatholicWealth, holding the wealth-specific figures -- these are NOT interchangeable, a developer must use the correct one for the tax type being computed. Only 'Ulmiz' (see quirk above) has no parish record at all in either confession's dataset; every other municipality including 'Fetigny-Menieres' (catholic parish 'Fetigny-Menieres' at 10.0% income/15.0% wealth, reformed parish 'Estavayer-le-Lac' at 9.0%/20.0%) has church data.

DEDUCTIONS AND OTHER MECHANISMS NOT ENCODED IN THIS DATASET (flagged for completeness, applied upstream of these brackets): substantial social deductions reduce taxable income before the income bracket table applies (e.g. CHF 8'600-9'600 per minor/student/apprentice child, CHF 4'100-5'100 modest-income deductions, CHF 2'500 wheelchair-user deduction, etc., all under Art. 36 LICD) and reduce taxable wealth before the wealth bracket table applies (CHF 55'000 single / CHF 105'000 married personal exemption, phasing down as wealth rises, Art. 61 LICD) -- these deductions are NOT part of incomeTaxBrackets/wealthTaxBrackets above and must be applied by the calculator as a prior step. Separately, FR has entirely distinct flat-rate schedules (not part of this dataset) for: capital payments from pension funds ('prestations en capital', 1-5% tiered by amount, Art. 39 LICD), real-estate capital gains ('gains immobiliers', 10-22% sliding by holding period, Art. 51 LICD), and liquidation profits for retiring self-employed persons (Art. 38b LICD, min. 6%).
